title: YOCO: A Hybrid In-Memory Computing Architecture with 8-bit Sub-PetaOps/W In-Situ Multiply Arithmetic for Large-Scale AI
problem: Analog in-memory computing (AiMC) requires efficient 8-bit multiply operations for AI accelerators with high energy efficiency and throughput.
motivation: AI inference demands extreme efficiency; analog computing avoids costly analog-to-digital conversions in the computational path.
method: YOCO proposes in-situ multiply arithmetic (IMA) using charge-domain computation and time-domain accumulation, combined with hybrid ReRAM-SRAM memory to balance efficiency and density. An IMC-friendly attention pipeline accelerates transformer inference.
key_novelty: 8-bit in-situ multiply arithmetic achieving 123.8 TOPS/W via efficient charge-domain compute and time-domain accumulation.
contributions: Novel 8-bit in-situ multiply arithmetic with 123.8 TOPS/W energy efficiency and 34.9 TOPS throughput
Hybrid ReRAM-SRAM memory architecture balancing computational efficiency and storage density
IMC-friendly attention computing flow with optimized pipeline for transformer acceleration
3.9-19.9x energy efficiency improvement and 6.8-33.6x throughput improvement over SOTA baselines across CNN/transformer models
limitations: Evaluation limited to 10 CNN/transformer models; generalization to other workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: Hybrid analog in-memory compute for efficient transformer inference
